children.title: Value Acquisition and Testing in Autonomous Systems

detail.title: Value Acquisition and Testing in Autonomous Systems
detail.summary: Autonomous systems often employ inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) to infer preference-based value systems. This process is inherently susceptible to path dependence, where stochastic initial learning phases influence final policy convergence, potentially leading to divergent value outcomes even with identical base environments.
detail.reason: Synthesizing available evidence on preference learning and reinforcement dynamics to support the hypothesis of emergent divergence.

detail.title: Value Acquisition and Testing in Autonomous Systems
detail.summary: This revision incorporates findings regarding the role of scalarization and information processing in value divergence across autonomous agents. Agents with identical initial conditions exhibit divergent behavioral outcomes when the transformation of environmental inputs—specifically reward scalarization—introduces path dependency.
detail.reason: Updating synthesis to include new evidence on agent processing mechanisms.
